title: One-key schedules for multi-round single-permutation Even--Mansour
summary: For every round count above two, find one-master-key schedules that give single-permutation Even--Mansour the optimal query-security exponent.

formal_statement.body: For every fixed integer $r>2$, let an $r$-round Even--Mansour cipher reuse one public random $n$-bit permutation in every round and derive all $r+1$ round keys deterministically from one uniformly random $n$-bit master key. Find explicit nondegenerate conditions on the key schedule, together with schedules satisfying them, under which the cipher is strong-PRP secure against $\widetilde O(2^{rn/(r+1)})$ adaptive two-sided cipher and permutation queries, or prove that this target is impossible for some $r$ under the same one-key and one-permutation restrictions.

scope.domain: Provable strong-PRP security of multi-round single-permutation Even--Mansour with minimal key material
assumptions: One public random n-bit permutation is reused in every round
All r+1 round keys are deterministic functions of one uniformly random n-bit master key
The adversary may query the cipher and public permutation adaptively in both directions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later proofs attain the target for three rounds and then arbitrary rounds with one reused permutation but independent random round keys. Conditions deriving every round key from a single n-bit master key while retaining the target for every r>2 remain unknown.

progress.summary: The source asks for sufficient one-master-key schedule conditions attaining the optimal exponent for every round count above two while reusing one permutation.
The three-round target is proved for a single reused permutation under independent random round keys, relaxing the source's one-master-key restriction.

progress.summary: The optimal arbitrary-round exponent is proved with a single reused permutation, but the proof still assumes independent random round keys.
